text: During the synthetic atmospheric campaign, instrument AX-41 measured aerosol optical depth at 550 nanometers. The reported value was 0.18.
Instrument AX-14 was used in a separate aerosol-monitoring experiment. At 550 nanometers, AX-14 reported an aerosol optical depth of 0.21.
The AX-41 atmospheric instrument requires periodic calibration using reference filters. Calibration corrects detector drift but does not itself provide an aerosol optical depth measurement.
The AX-410 sensor is a later member of the AX instrument family. During a synthetic test it measured aerosol optical depth of 0.16 at 550 nanometers.
The AX-41B prototype recorded an aerosol optical depth of 0.19 during laboratory validation. Its optical configuration differs slightly from the original AX-41.
Dynamic Graph CNN, or DGCNN, performs point-cloud learning with EdgeConv layers. Neighborhood graphs are recomputed dynamically in feature space as the network processes the point cloud.
PointNet++ extends PointNet through hierarchical sampling and grouping. Local neighborhoods are aggregated at increasingly large spatial scales.
PointNet applies shared multilayer perceptrons independently to individual points and obtains a global representation through a symmetric max-pooling operation.

Graph Attention Networks operate on graph-structured data by assigning learned attention weights to neighboring nodes. The graph structure is normally provided rather than reconstructed dynamically after each feature transformation.
GeoCD is a geometry-aware distance for point clouds. Instead of relying purely on ambient Euclidean proximity, it approximates intrinsic geodesic structure using propagation over local neighborhoods.
Chamfer distance compares two point sets using nearest-neighbor distances in both directions. Standard Chamfer distance measures proximity in ambient Euclidean space.

Earth Mover's Distance measures the minimum transport cost needed to transform one point distribution into another. It captures global assignment structure but is computationally more expensive than Chamfer distance.

ModelNet40-E is an uncertainty-aware benchmark for point-cloud classification. It introduces LiDAR-inspired corruptions and supports evaluation of robustness, calibration, uncertainty estimation, and error detection.
ModelNet40 is a collection of synthetic CAD models commonly used for three-dimensional object classification. The traditional benchmark primarily evaluates classification accuracy.
ScanObjectNN contains real scanned objects and is often used to evaluate point-cloud models under more realistic sensing conditions than synthetic CAD datasets.
CRISPR-Cas9 uses a guide RNA to direct the Cas9 nuclease toward a complementary DNA sequence. Cas9 creates a targeted DNA break that can be used for genome editing.
Base editing is derived from CRISPR technology but can change selected DNA bases without producing a conventional double-strand DNA break.

Prime editing combines a modified Cas9 protein with a reverse transcriptase and a specialized guide RNA. It can write new genetic information without requiring the same double-strand break used by standard CRISPR-Cas9.
NIRCam is the Near Infrared Camera aboard the James Webb Space Telescope. It provides imaging at near-infrared wavelengths and supports observations of galaxies, stars, and exoplanets.
NIRSpec is the Near Infrared Spectrograph aboard the James Webb Space Telescope. It separates incoming near-infrared light into spectra rather than primarily producing direct images.
MIRI is the Mid-Infrared Instrument aboard the James Webb Space Telescope. It provides both imaging and spectroscopic capabilities at longer infrared wavelengths than NIRCam and NIRSpec.
The transit method detects exoplanets by measuring recurring decreases in stellar brightness when a planet crosses the visible disk of its host star.
The radial-velocity method searches for periodic shifts in stellar spectral lines caused by the gravitational influence of an orbiting planet on its host star.
Gravitational microlensing can reveal planets when a foreground planetary system temporarily magnifies the light of a more distant background star.
The synthetic catalyst ZK-91 reduces the activation-energy barrier of chemical reaction R17. In the test experiment it increased the reaction rate without being consumed.
Catalyst ZK-19 was evaluated for reaction R17 but produced only a small change in reaction rate. It was not the catalyst associated with the large reduction in activation energy.
Catalyst ZK-91 was also tested on reaction R71. In that experiment its effect was weak and the reaction kinetics remained nearly unchanged.
Principal component analysis reduces dimensionality by projecting observations onto orthogonal directions ordered according to the amount of variance they explain.
t-SNE is a nonlinear dimensionality-reduction technique designed primarily for visualization. It attempts to preserve local neighborhood relationships in a low-dimensional embedding.
UMAP constructs a graph representation of local relationships in high-dimensional data and optimizes a low-dimensional embedding that approximately preserves this structure.

BERT learns bidirectional contextual representations with a transformer encoder. Its original pretraining objective includes masked language modeling, where hidden tokens are predicted using information from both surrounding directions.
GPT-style language models are autoregressive transformers. They predict subsequent tokens from preceding context rather than using the bidirectional masked-token objective associated with BERT.
T5 treats many natural-language tasks as text-to-text problems. Its encoder-decoder transformer is pretrained using corrupted text spans that must be reconstructed.

Retrieval-augmented generation retrieves external evidence before producing an answer. Retrieved passages are supplied to the language model so that generation can be grounded in information outside the model parameters.
BM25 is a lexical information-retrieval method. Its scoring function combines term occurrence, inverse document frequency, term-frequency saturation, and document-length normalization.

Reciprocal Rank Fusion combines multiple ranked result lists without requiring the original retrieval scores to share a common scale. Each document receives contributions determined by its position in each ranking.

Dense retrieval maps queries and documents into vector representations. Similarity between those representations allows semantically related passages to be retrieved even when they do not share exactly the same vocabulary.
Type Ia supernovae can be standardized using correlations in their light curves. Their inferred luminosities allow astronomers to estimate cosmological distances from observed brightness.
Cepheid variable stars exhibit a relationship between pulsation period and intrinsic luminosity. This relation makes them important distance indicators within relatively nearby astronomical systems.
Baryon acoustic oscillations provide a characteristic clustering scale that can be used as a standard ruler for studies of cosmic expansion.

The LIGO observatories measure gravitational waves using kilometer-scale laser interferometers. A passing gravitational wave produces extremely small changes in the relative lengths of perpendicular interferometer arms.
Pulsar timing arrays search for very low-frequency gravitational waves by monitoring correlated changes in the arrival times of radio pulses from many millisecond pulsars.
Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy. Chlorophyll absorbs radiation while carbon dioxide and water provide material used to synthesize carbohydrates.
Chemosynthesis produces organic compounds using energy released by chemical reactions rather than sunlight. Some microorganisms use this process in deep-ocean environments.
Methane absorbs infrared radiation and contributes to the greenhouse effect. Although its atmospheric concentration is much lower than that of carbon dioxide, it is an important greenhouse gas.
In a synthetic climate dataset, an imaginary monitoring station recorded annual average carbon dioxide concentrations of 400 ppm in 2015 and 420 ppm in 2025.
The SARS-CoV-2 spike protein binds the ACE2 receptor on host cells and plays an important role in viral entry.
Influenza viruses use hemagglutinin to bind sialic-acid-containing receptors on host cells. This surface protein contributes to viral attachment and entry.
The Adam optimizer maintains exponentially decaying estimates of first and second moments of the gradient and uses them to adapt the learning rate for individual parameters.

Stochastic gradient descent updates model parameters using gradients computed from minibatches. Momentum can be added to smooth updates and accelerate optimization along persistent descent directions.

Dropout is a regularization method that randomly disables a subset of neural-network activations during training. This reduces reliance on particular feature combinations and can improve generalization.
Batch normalization normalizes intermediate activations using minibatch statistics during training and maintains running statistics for use during inference.
